title: Engineer Onramp Handoff Kit (compact draft)
content:
Purpose: lightweight, engineer-focused mini-deck + battlecard bundle to hand to platform/infra engineers during pilot conversations.

Audience: Platform engineers, integration architects, SREs on customer side; field SEs and platform sellers internally.

Top-line pitch (1 line): "Redwood gives your platform teams predictable per-request latency with cost levers you actually control — batching, KV caching, and safe fallbacks — so you can ship inference features without building the whole serving stack."

One-slide outline (for conversion into 4 slides):
- Slide 1: Problem framing — inconsistent latency, exploding token costs, black-box fallbacks. quick bullet examples from real prospects (search, summarization, reranking).
- Slide 2: How Redwood runs — unified API, routing policies, caching, quantization recommendations. small diagram note: runtime + control plane + routing -> predictable SLOs.
- Slide 3: Engineering guarantees & operations — per-route latency SLOs, canary rollouts, KV cache invalidation primitives, audit logs for Private. callout: Dedicated pools for consistent tail latency.
- Slide 4: Pilot checklist & next steps — simple 6-step integration: sample curl -> perf run -> tune batch -> add rolling canary -> validate eval set -> commit to reserved capacity.

Battlecard (compact):
- Champion profile: Platform engineer who needs low tail-latency and predictable cost for many small requests (embedding lookup, classification).
- Key objection 1: "We can self-host cheaper."
  * Short rebuttal: "Maybe at massive scale, but we handle kernel selection, batching heuristics, KV cache, and model fallback out of the box. Early pilot numbers show 30–45% lower per-token infra cost vs naive self-host + significantly lower tail latency due to continuous batching."
  * Backup evidence: pointer to internal perf summary (INF-7021).
- Key objection 2: "We need deterministic privacy / air-gapped options."
  * Rebuttal: Redwood Private + optional on-prem package + KMS/HSM integrations. Mention audit logs and SOC controls.
- Key objection 3: "What about quality regression when quantizing?"
  * Rebuttal: Redwood Optimize makes model and quantization recommendations by workload and includes eval hooks; we can run candidate quantization on a small test corpus during pilot.

Technical FAQ snippets for SE to use:
- Q: "How do fallbacks work?"
  A: Policy-driven routing; if model variant unavailable, router picks nearest-compatible variant (quantized or smaller), with per-request tags so caller knows fallback occurred.
- Q: "How to measure true cost?"
  A: Console shows token-level cost breakdown, per-route and per-model. Provide a sample query showing 0.6ms token compute + 1.2ms queueing on 80% load.
- Q: "Access from private VPC?"
  A: Private control plane + customer-managed networking; we ship a lightweight sidecar for ingress in on-prem installs.

Integration troubleshooting checklist (quick):
- Confirm TLS + client certs for Private installs
- Validate KV cache TTLs for your workload (default 2h)
- Run short perf run at target QPS for 15 minutes, capture p50/p95/p99
- Turn on prefix caching and measure token savings

Sample short scripts (to convert into slide speaker notes):
- Opening line for SE: "Hi — I want to show how we get predictable latency and control cost without you having to tune kernels or implement your own batching layer."
- Quick demo flow: 1) curl simple text generation 2) show tokens and latency in console 3) flip to routing policy to show canary -> switch traffic -> rollback.

Open questions / placeholders (to resolve before final deck):
- Need up-to-date cost comparison table for T4x vs self-hosted with Mistral/LLM variants (ask infra for batch/job numbers).
- One-liner SLA for Dedicated (confirm legal phrasing).
- Include two short customer quotes (ask CS for anonymized blips).

Action items (owner tags inline):
- Ethan: pull 3 perf runs for embedding workloads (due 2025-01-20)
- Marisol: draft one-liner SLA blurb and legal check-in (due 2025-01-18)
- Tom: create demo script and automated perf runner (due 2025-01-25)
- Priya: iterate slide drafts and hand to design for microdeck layout (due 2025-01-30)

Slack & refs: see #platform-sellers thread (SLACK msg id: C0345X2) and Confluence page INFER-847 for longer playbook.

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep slides under 6 for quick field use.
- Emphasize: "we own the hard infra work — you get a predictable API and cost controls".
- Avoid marketing-y buzz in engineer-facing slides; prefer metrics, config knobs, and a 6-step pilot road map.

End of draft. Convert to 4 slide pdf + one-page battlecard cheat sheet for SEs.
